texts: Following surgical correction of pulmonary stenosis, there is often a residual gradient: A.
A small gradient commonly persists after valvotomy, from a small annulus or from muscle in the outflow tract, and much of the infundibular part falls as the hypertrophy regresses.

Outcomes in pulmonary atresia with intact septum are poorer and depend on the size of the right ventricle: patients reach a biventricular, one-and-a-half or single-ventricle repair, and most now survive to a definitive operation.
